sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Preset tables and imports
sections.what: Loads the typing and path tools and defines two preset tables: model choices for different needs, and a set of tuning values.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the recommendations in one place for the export routes to show.
sections.watch_out: The presets are not read when the agent picks its model, so editing them does not change what the app uses.

sections.name: Settings (part 1)
sections.title: Settings fields
sections.what: Lists every setting with its default: OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, SharePoint, vector store, app, cache, and agent values. Each is read from the environment variable of the same name.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps secrets out of the code and lets each machine set its own values.
sections.watch_out: The default CORS value allows any website to call the backend, and the secret defaults are empty, so missing keys are not reported here.

sections.name: Settings: get_model_recommendation
sections.title: Settings helpers and global object
sections.what: Provides a helper that returns a model preset for a use case, creates the settings folders, and builds the shared settings object when the file loads.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared settings object is simpler than reading the environment everywhere.
sections.watch_out: The settings object is built on import, so a folder permission problem appears as soon as any backend file loads this one, and an unknown use case silently returns the accuracy preset.

summary: Reads all backend settings from the environment or a .env file and holds two preset tables for model choices and tuning values.
purpose: Gives every backend file one shared settings object.
why: Likely reason: keeps settings and secrets out of the code.
how: The preset tables are plain lists of values. A Settings class lists each setting with its default, and values from the .env file or the environment replace those defaults. When the file is first imported, it creates the vector store, cache, documents, logs, and exports folders.
outputs: A settings object used across the backend, and two preset tables.
risks: The default CORS value allows any website to call the backend. Defaults differ from the sample .env. Folders are created the moment this file is first imported, even in a script that does not need them.
debug: If a setting is ignored, check that the .env file is in the folder the program starts from and that the name matches. Printing the settings object shows the values that were loaded.
